Introduced By: Vice President AJ Tsang this  2nd day of November in the Year 2018

Sponsored By: Executive Secretary Aspen Williams of the Executive Board

Senator Lauren Paulet of the Sophomore Class

Referred to the senate by the Committee on Finance which recommends its Passage/failure by a vote of X to X.

Be it enacted by the Senate of the Student Government Association of The Johns Hopkins University assembled that:

SECTION 1. TITLE.

This proposal is to benefit the funding of the Blue Jay Blackout tailgate to take place November, 10, 2018.

SECTION 2. DEFINITIONS AND DESCRIPTION.

SGA — The term “SGA” shall refer to the Student Government Association of The Johns Hopkins University.

JHU, Hopkins — The terms “JHU” and “Hopkins” shall refer to the Johns Hopkins University.

SAAC — The term “SAAC” shall refer to Student-Athlete Advisory Committee.

Tailgate — The term “Tailgate” shall refer to the Blue Jay Blackout Tailgate.

SECTION 3. PURPOSE AND DEVELOPMENT.

FINDINGS

Background

Sporting events are an integral part of the college experience and something that SAAC hopes to further develop in years to come. As a way of showing our Hopkins pride and further connecting the student body not only with each other but also with the university, SAAC plans on building the tradition of engaged spectatorship at sporting events—a tradition that is introduced every year as the incoming class congregates around Homewood field during orientation, but one that is often ill-executed. The tailgate is intended to provide a positive and engaging experience to foster a supportive community.

Overview & Objectives

The tailgate is a part of SAAC’s newly developed “Pack the Nest” initiative to promote awareness and support for varsity athletics on campus. With the goal of filling the stands at major sporting events throughout each competition season, SAAC hopes to provide an opportunity for the entire student body to come together and to build school spirit.

To accomplish this, the tailgate will encourage the student body to rally behind our Blue Jays and participate in a variety of ways. The program will include engaging activities and friendly competition, all of which serve to further connect friendships and to foster a sense of community. Catering lunch before the game and giving away t-shirts will incentivize students to take a healthy break from their work to enjoy a game-day tradition.

 Senate

The Johns Hopkins University

{ S. Resolution 18-19, XX }

A Resolution in Opposition of the Johns Hopkins University Police Department

Introduced By: Senator Alexander Forlenza of the Freshman Class and considered this 7th day of April in the Year 2019

Sponsored By:

Senator Sam Mollin of the Sophomore Class and Senator Claire Gorman of the junior Class

Referred to the senate by Civic Engagement which recommends its Passage by a vote of 5 to 0.

Whereas Section II of the Johns Hopkins Undergraduate Student Government Association’s Constitution states, “The purpose of the SGA is to protect and improve the rights, opportunities, and quality of life for every undergraduate student at the Johns Hopkins University;”

Whereas Section III of the Johns Hopkins Undergraduate Student Government Association’s Constitution states, “The authority of SGA is derived from the students of the Johns Hopkins University and collectively recognized by the University President and other administrators.”

Whereas  Private Police forces at other American universities have had violent histories

Last spring at the University of Chicago a student, in the midst of a mental crisis, was shot by one of the university's police officers.[1]

At UCLA, in 2013, a Judge was brutalized by UCLA officers nowhere near UCLA property[2]

In 2012, an 18-year-old student at the University of South Alabama was killed by a school police officer without ever being within 4 feet of the officer[3]

Whereas the establishment of a Johns Hopkins Police Department, hereinafter private police force, will create new dangers, both physical and mental, to the students of Johns Hopkins

Whereas Private University Police forces across the nation have had a very racist history with trends of stopping black people significantly more than any other group[4], stronger use of force against black people[5][6], and generally giving black people a hard time when going about regular activities like napping.[7]

Whereas the establishment of a private police force will create a fearful environment for many black students[8], and it will also negatively affect everyone on campus who comes from a background of distrust towards the police be it because of race, religion, or sexual identity.

An Act Funding Transportation to the 2019 Washington D.C. Monument Quilt

Introduced By: Executive President AJ Tsang and considered this 30th day of April in the Year 2019

Sponsored By: Executive Vice President Miranda Bannister of the Executive Board

 Senator Madelynn Wellons of the Junior Class

Referred to the senate by the Committee on Finance which recommends its Passage/failure by a vote of X to X.

Composed with extensive assistance from Lauren Bernard, APO officer.

Be it enacted by the Senate of the Student Government Association of The Johns Hopkins University assembled that:

SECTION 1. TITLE.

This Act may be referred to as the “Monument Quilt Transportation Act of 2019.”

SECTION 2. DEFINITIONS.

SGA — The term “SGA” shall refer to the Student Government Association of The Johns Hopkins University.

JHU, Hopkins — The terms “JHU” and “Hopkins” shall refer to the Johns Hopkins University.

APO — The term “APO” shall refer to Alphi Phi Omega.

SARU — The term “SARU” shall refer to the Sexual Assault Resource Unit.

SECTION 3. FINDINGS AND PURPOSES.

FINDINGS

Background on Project

SARU and APO would like to sponsor a JHMI bus to transport any Hopkins undergraduate to Washington D.C. on June 1st, 2019 for the Monument Quilt final display.

The Monument Quilt is a project under a local Baltimore nonprofit called FORCE that provides an outlet for survivors of sexual assault and allies via the healing means of quilt-making.

Since Spring 2016, 185 members of APO have volunteered together more than 2,000 hours to help put 3,000 quilt squares submitted from across the country together, and more than 25 of these volunteers have indicated they would like to attend on June 1st.

In addition, SARU has heavily contributed to providing safe healing spaces for Hopkins undergraduates at Homewood and would like to provide equal opportunity to members of both their organizations and the Homewood community at-large so any undergraduate who would like to be there in support of sexual assault survivors may go.

SARU and APO have been advised by the Title IX Coordinator that a JHMI would cost $800 and would likely need to be facilitated through the Office of Student Leadership & Involvement, should SGA funding be received.

Project Costs

SARU and APO estimate that a bus would cost $800.

Financial Assurance

June 1st, 2019 is within the 2018/2019 calendar year and can thus be considered an expense for which this Senate can approve.
